points.name: 〜ものの (mono no) — although / even though (disappointing concession)
points.shortDescription: Concedes something is true, but the result is disappointing or doesn't meet expectations.
points.formation: Plain form + ものの + disappointing or contrary outcome
points.explanation:
ものの is a formal, literary concessive — 'although / even though' — with a built-in undercurrent of disappointment or unfulfilled expectation. 準備[じゅんび]はしたものの、本番[ほんばん]では緊張[きんちょう]してうまくできなかった: 'Although I had prepared, when it came to the real thing I got nervous and couldn't do well.' The preparation happened; the expected payoff didn't arrive. That gap between effort and result, or between intention and outcome, is the emotional core of ものの.

If you've been using のに (even though) for this kind of contrast, you know the territory — ものの occupies the same space but at a higher register, suited to writing, polished speech, and formal contexts where のに would feel too colloquial. The main clause almost always conveys regret, disappointment, or ironic contrast. ものの tends to focus on the speaker's own unfulfilled efforts or intentions; when you want to express frustration at an external situation that didn't reward what was done, のに can feel more immediate and natural.
rules: Plain form + ものの = although / even though (result falls short of expectation)
The main clause presents an outcome that disappoints or contradicts the expectation set up
Formal/literary — used in writing, polished speech; のに covers the same ground more colloquially
Often about the speaker's own unfulfilled efforts, intentions, or hopes
Main clause tone is almost always: regret, disappointment, or ironic contrast

points.flashcardAnswer: Concedes something is true, but the result is disappointing or doesn't meet expectations.

practice.prompt: What does 〜ものの mean?
choices: because / therefore
although / while it's true that X — concedes X but contrasts with Y (which is different or less than expected)
just because X
the fact that X
practice.explanation: 〜ものの = although / while X is true (concessive). 合格[ごうかく]したものの、あまり嬉[うれ]しくない = although I passed, I'm not very happy. Concedes the first clause but introduces a contrasting or unexpected result.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although I bought the gym membership, I've never gone'?
choices: ジムの会員権[かいいんけん]を買[か]ったものの、一度[いちど]も行[い]っていない。
ジムの会員権[かいいんけん]を買[か]ったが、一度[いちど]も行[い]っていない。
ジムの会員権[かいいんけん]を買[か]ったけれど、一度[いちど]も行[い]っていない。
ジムの会員権[かいいんけん]を買[か]ったにもかかわらず、一度[いちど]も行[い]っていない。
practice.explanation: Verb past + ものの: 買[か]った + ものの = although (I) bought. 一度[いちど]も行[い]っていない = have never gone. ものの concedes the purchase but contrasts with the non-use.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Although he studies every day, his grades don't improve'?
choices: 毎日[まいにち]勉強[べんきょう]しているものの、成績[せいせき]が上[あ]がらない。
毎日[まいにち]勉強[べんきょう]しているが、成績[せいせき]が上[あ]がらない。
毎日[まいにち]勉強[べんきょう]しているけれど、成績[せいせき]が上[あ]がらない。
毎日[まいにち]勉強[べんきょう]しているにもかかわらず、成績[せいせき]が上[あ]がらない。
practice.explanation: Verb te-iru + ものの: 勉強[べんきょう]している + ものの = although (he) studies. 成績[せいせき]が上[あ]がらない = grades don't improve. Contrast between effort and result.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although we have a plan, we don't know how to execute it'?
choices: 計画[けいかく]はあるものの、実行方法[じっこうほうほう]がわからない。
計画[けいかく]はあるが、実行方法[じっこうほうほう]がわからない。
計画[けいかく]はあるけれど、実行方法[じっこうほうほう]がわからない。
計画[けいかく]はあるにもかかわらず、実行方法[じっこうほうほう]がわからない。
practice.explanation: Plain form + ものの: ある + ものの = although there is. 実行方法[じっこうほうほう]がわからない = don't know how to execute. Concedes plan existence, contrasts with execution difficulty.

practice.prompt: What FORMS can precede ものの?
choices: Only verb past-form — textbooks treat this as an absolute rule, regardless of context or politeness level.
Verb dict/past/te-iru, い-adj plain, な-adj な/だった, Noun + ではある/だった — essentially plain forms + ものの
Only noun + ものの
Only い-adj + ものの
practice.explanation: ものの attaches to plain forms: 行[い]った + ものの (past verb), 行[い]く + ものの (dict verb), 安[やす]い + ものの (い-adj), 便利[べんり]なものの (な-adj), 学生[がくせい]ではあるものの (noun). Wide compatibility across parts of speech.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although the food is delicious, it's a bit expensive'?
choices: 料理[りょうり]はおいしいものの、少[すこ]し高[たか]い。
料理[りょうり]はおいしいが、少[すこ]し高[たか]い。
料理[りょうり]はおいしいけれど、少[すこ]し高[たか]い。
料理[りょうり]はおいしいにもかかわらず、少[すこ]し高[たか]い。
practice.explanation: い-adj + ものの: おいしい + ものの = although (it's) delicious. 少[すこ]し高[たか]い = a bit expensive. ものの concedes the positive (delicious) but notes the drawback (expensive).

practice.prompt: Which means 'Although the technology is advanced, it's difficult to use'?
choices: 技術[ぎじゅつ]は進[すす]んでいるものの、使[つか]い方[かた]が難[むずか]しい。
技術[ぎじゅつ]は進[すす]んでいるが、使[つか]い方[かた]が難[むずか]しい。
技術[ぎじゅつ]は進[すす]んでいるけれど、使[つか]い方[かた]が難[むずか]しい。
技術[ぎじゅつ]は進[すす]んでいるにもかかわらず、使[つか]い方[かた]が難[むずか]しい。
practice.explanation: Verb te-iru + ものの: 進[すす]んでいる + ものの = although it's advanced. 使[つか]い方[かた]が難[むずか]しい = difficult to use. ものの presents the contrast between advanced technology and usability difficulty.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although I applied for the job, I don't have much confidence'?
choices: 仕事[しごと]に応募[おうぼ]したものの、あまり自信[じしん]がない。

仕事[しごと]に応募[おうぼ]したけれど、あまり自信[じしん]がない。
仕事[しごと]に応募[おうぼ]したにもかかわらず、あまり自信[じしん]がない。
practice.explanation: Verb past + ものの: 応募[おうぼ]した + ものの = although (I) applied. あまり自信[じしん]がない = don't have much confidence. ものの concedes the action but notes the internal state contrast.

practice.prompt: ものの vs. が (contrastive が) — what's the difference?
choices: They are identical
ものの is more formal/literary, suitable for written Japanese and formal speech; が is more casual and conversational. Both mean 'although/but'
ものの can only be used in speech, regardless of context or politeness level — this is true in both spoken and written Japanese.
が is more emphatic
practice.explanation: ものの is more formal and literary. It's common in essays, reports, and formal writing. Contrastive が is natural in both speech and writing. Both mean 'although/but' — choose based on formality level.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although I understand the theory, applying it is difficult'?
choices: 理論[りろん]はわかるものの、実践[じっせん]するのは難[むずか]しい。
理論[りろん]はわかるが、実践[じっせん]するのは難[むずか]しい。
理論[りろん]はわかるけれど、実践[じっせん]するのは難[むずか]しい。
理論[りろん]はわかるにもかかわらず、実践[じっせん]するのは難[むずか]しい。
practice.explanation: Plain verb + ものの: わかる + ものの = although (I) understand. 実践[じっせん]するのは難[むずか]しい = applying it is difficult. ものの contrasts theoretical understanding with practical difficulty.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Although she apologized, the relationship didn't recover'?

謝[あやま]ったが、関係[かんけい]は回復[かいふく]しなかった。
謝[あやま]ったけれど、関係[かんけい]は回復[かいふく]しなかった。
謝[あやま]ったにもかかわらず、関係[かんけい]は回復[かいふく]しなかった。
practice.explanation: Verb past + ものの: 謝[あやま]った + ものの = although (she) apologized. 関係[かんけい]は回復[かいふく]しなかった = relationship didn't recover. ものの presents the gap between the apology and its ineffectiveness.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although the salary is low, the work is rewarding'?
choices: 給料[きゅうりょう]は低[ひく]いものの、やりがいのある仕事[しごと]だ。
給料[きゅうりょう]は低[ひく]いが、やりがいのある仕事[しごと]だ。

給料[きゅうりょう]は低[ひく]いにもかかわらず、やりがいのある仕事[しごと]だ。
practice.explanation: い-adj + ものの: 低[ひく]い + ものの = although (the salary is) low. やりがいのある仕事[しごと]だ = the work is rewarding. ものの concedes the drawback but notes the compensating advantage.

practice.prompt: ものの vs. にもかかわらず — which is MORE emphatic in contrast?
choices: They are identical
にもかかわらず is MORE emphatic (despite X, against expectation); ものの is softer (while it's true that X, nonetheless Y)
ものの is more emphatic
They cannot be compared — this is true in both spoken and written Japanese.
practice.explanation: にもかかわらず = despite X (stronger, against expectation): 努力[どりょく]にもかかわらず失敗[しっぱい]した (despite effort, failed — stronger contrast). ものの = although (softer, less emphatic): 努力[どりょく]したものの失敗[しっぱい]した (although I tried, failed — gentler concession).

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although I was accepted to university, I haven't decided what to study'?
choices: 大学[だいがく]に合格[ごうかく]したものの、何[なに]を勉強[べんきょう]するか決[き]めていない。
大学[だいがく]に合格[ごうかく]したが、何[なに]を勉強[べんきょう]するか決[き]めていない。
大学[だいがく]に合格[ごうかく]したけれど、何[なに]を勉強[べんきょう]するか決[き]めていない。
大学[だいがく]に合格[ごうかく]したにもかかわらず、何[なに]を勉強[べんきょう]するか決[き]めていない。

practice.prompt: Which means 'Although it's convenient, there are some concerns about privacy'?

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although I set the alarm, I still overslept'?
choices: アラームをセットしたものの、寝坊[ねぼう]してしまった。

アラームをセットしたけれど、寝坊[ねぼう]してしまった。

practice.prompt: Which best characterizes ものの usage?
choices: Strong causal connection, and the rule applies to every sentence type — and this holds in every register, formal or casual.
Concessive construction: 'While X is acknowledged, Y introduces a contrasting fact, gap, or unexpected outcome'
Conditional connection
Additive connection
practice.explanation: ものの = concessive: speaker acknowledges X as true but introduces Y as a qualification, contrast, or gap. 合格[ごうかく]したものの準備[じゅんび]が足[た]りない = while I passed, my preparation is still lacking. The contrast is often an internal inconsistency, unmet expectation, or qualifying reality.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although I started the project, I'm not sure it will work out'?
choices: プロジェクトを始[はじ]めたものの、うまくいくか自信[じしん]がない。

practice.prompt: Which means 'Although the product is highly rated, the price puts people off'?
choices: 製品[せいひん]は高評価[こうひょうか]なものの、値段[ねだん]が高[たか]くて敬遠[けいえん]される。
製品[せいひん]は高評価[こうひょうか]だが、値段[ねだん]が高[たか]くて敬遠[けいえん]される。

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although I had studied abroad, my English didn't improve much'?
choices: 留学[りゅうがく]したものの、英語[えいご]はあまり上達[じょうたつ]しなかった。
留学[りゅうがく]したが、英語[えいご]はあまり上達[じょうたつ]しなかった。
留学[りゅうがく]したけれど、英語[えいご]はあまり上達[じょうたつ]しなかった。
留学[りゅうがく]したにもかかわらず、英語[えいご]はあまり上達[じょうたつ]しなかった。
practice.explanation: Verb past + ものの: 留学[りゅうがく]した + ものの = although (I) studied abroad. あまり上達[じょうたつ]しなかった = didn't improve much. ものの captures the gap between the expectation (studying abroad → fluency) and the disappointing reality.

points.name: 〜とはいえ (to wa ie) — that said / even so / nonetheless
points.shortDescription: Acknowledges a stated fact but presents a contrasting reality or qualification.
points.formation: Plain form / Noun / な-adj + とはいえ + contrasting point
points.explanation:
とはいえ means 'that said,' 'even so,' or 'nonetheless' — it acknowledges that the first statement is true, then pivots to a qualification or contrast. 暖[あたた]かくなったとはいえ、まだコートが必要[ひつよう]ですよ: 'That said, it has gotten warmer — you still need a coat.' The speaker isn't denying the warmth; they're adding an important qualifier.

What sets とはいえ apart from simpler connectors like でも or しかし is its explicit concession: rather than simply changing direction, it first grants the preceding point, then limits or qualifies it. The logic is: 'I accept X; but even granting X, Y is still true.' The etymology makes this visible: と (quotation) + は (topic marker) + いえ (even if one grants / even conceding that).

Formal and literary, it appears regularly in written analysis, essays, and formal speech. The slightly more casual variant とはいっても does the same work in less formal contexts — a useful pair to know.
rules: Plain form / Noun / な-adj + とはいえ = that said / even so (concedes first, then contrasts)
First clause is acknowledged as true; second clause qualifies or limits it
Formal and literary — appears in writing and formal speech
Concedes more explicitly than しかし — 'I grant that X, but still Y'
Related: とはいっても (even though one says so — slightly more casual)

points.flashcardAnswer: Acknowledges a stated fact but presents a contrasting reality or qualification.

practice.prompt: What does 〜とはいえ mean?
choices: because X / therefore Y
although / even though / granted that X — concedes X but introduces Y as an important qualification or contrast
needless to say
as long as X
practice.explanation: 〜とはいえ = although / even though / granted that. 春[はる]とはいえ、まだ寒[さむ]い = although it's spring, it's still cold. Acknowledges X as true (spring), but qualifies it with a contrasting reality (still cold).

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although it's a holiday, the shop is busy'?

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Although it's cheap, the quality is good'?

practice.prompt: What FORMS can precede とはいえ?
choices: Only noun

choices: 有名[ゆうめい]だとはいえ、彼[かれ]は質素[しっそ]な生活[せいかつ]を送[おく]っている。
有名[ゆうめい]だが、彼[かれ]は質素[しっそ]な生活[せいかつ]を送[おく]っている。

points.name: 〜ものだから (mono dakara) — because / the reason is (explanatory/excusing)
points.shortDescription: Explains or excuses an outcome by citing the reason — often with a defensive or explanatory tone.
points.formation: Plain form + ものだから / もので (more casual)
points.explanation:
ものだから (and its casual short form もので) is the explanatory grammar of 'I couldn't help it' — it cites a cause for something that happened, with the implicit frame that the cause was a natural, strong, or somewhat compelling impulse rather than a deliberate choice. うれしかったものだから、つい笑[わら]ってしまいました: 'Because I was so happy, I just couldn't help smiling.' The happiness was genuine and irresistible; the smile was the natural outcome.

Compare with plain から and ので, which are neutral about whether the cause was controllable. ものだから/もので adds the nuance of 'this was a compelling natural impulse, I was somewhat carried along by it' — which is exactly why it appears so often in apologies and self-explanations.

Practically speaking, ものだから is almost always used when the speaker is explaining their own behavior or a past situation that turned out badly. It's almost never used to explain other people's behavior. Register: もので is casual spoken; ものですから is the polite formal version.
rules: Plain form + ものだから = because (used to explain or excuse one's own behavior/outcome)
Implies the cause was natural, strong, or beyond full control — softens the explanation
More personal and explanatory than から/ので; often in apologies or self-explanation
Short form: もので (casual spoken); ものですから (polite/formal spoken)
Almost always used about the speaker's own behavior — rarely about others'

points.flashcardAnswer: Explains or excuses an outcome by citing the reason — often with a defensive or explanatory tone.

practice.prompt: What does 〜ものだから mean?
choices: although / despite
because / since (used when explaining or justifying one's own actions or circumstances — often with a subjective or defensive tone)
just because X
as a result of X

Formal/polite causation

practice.explanation: ものだから carries a subjective explanatory tone: the speaker is justifying, apologizing, or explaining away their behavior or a situation. It's warmer and more personal than the neutral ので or から.

practice.prompt: ものだから vs. ので — what's the difference?
choices: They are identical
ものだから: more subjective, often self-justifying or explaining speaker's own situation (warmer, personal); ので: neutral, polite cause-and-effect
ものだから is more formal
ので can only be used in writing, and the rule applies to every sentence type — and this holds in every register, formal or casual.
practice.explanation: ものだから: 急[いそ]いでいるものだから (because I'm in a hurry — personal explanation/justification). ので: 急[いそ]いでいるので (because I'm in a hurry — neutral, polite). ものだから feels more personal and often implies the speaker is justifying or explaining away something.

practice.prompt: ものだから is most naturally used when the SUBJECT is...

practice.prompt: もんだから is a COLLOQUIAL variant of ものだから. Which context suits it?

choices: めったにないチャンスなものだから、迷[まよ]わず引[ひ]き受[う]けた。
めったにないチャンスだったから、迷[まよ]わず引[ひ]き受[う]けた。
めったにないチャンスだったので、迷[まよ]わず引[ひ]き受[う]けた。
めったにないチャンスだったけれど、迷[まよ]わず引[ひ]き受[う]けた。
practice.explanation: Noun + な + ものだから: めったにないチャンス + な + ものだから = because it's such a rare opportunity. 迷[まよ]わず引[ひ]き受[う]けた = accepted without hesitation. ものだから justifies the immediate acceptance.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Because the baby was sleeping, we talked quietly'?
choices: 赤[あか]ちゃんが眠[ねむ]っているものだから、静[しず]かに話[はな]した。
赤[あか]ちゃんが眠[ねむ]っていたから、静[しず]かに話[はな]した。
赤[あか]ちゃんが眠[ねむ]っていたので、静[しず]かに話[はな]した。
赤[あか]ちゃんが眠[ねむ]っていたけれど、静[しず]かに話[はな]した。
practice.explanation: Verb te-iru + ものだから: 眠[ねむ]っている + ものだから = because (the baby) is sleeping. 静[しず]かに話[はな]した = talked quietly. ものだから explains the quiet behavior with a situationally-aware tone.
